findings.claim: The plateau diagnosed in reports/ember-v0.0.25-plateau-analysis.json is broken. This is the first run since v0.0.16 in which the model measurably learned.
evidence: Expanded continuation rose 0.7534 -> 0.8151 and legacy continuation 0.8406 -> 0.8696, against v0.0.21-v0.0.25 which were flat or negative.
The three changes were made together: format parity in the curriculum, learning rate restored 1.8e-7 -> 1.2e-6, and removal of the failure-neighbour oversampling.

findings.claim: Copy errors are now approximately independent across token positions, so there is no single systematic failure mode left to remove.
evidence: Mean continuation length is 69/9 = 7.67 tokens on the legacy battery.
Independent per-token errors at 0.8151 predict an exact-copy rate of 0.2086; the measured rate is 0.2222.
At the v0.0.20 baseline the same model predicted 0.1141 against a measured 0.1889, i.e. errors were clustered then and are scattered now.
findings.consequence: Exact copy is now limited multiplicatively by sequence length rather than by one broken structure. Per-token accuracy of 0.9262 is required for the legacy 0.5556 gate, up from 0.8151.

findings.claim: The checkpoint selector very likely chose the worse of the two candidates.
evidence: Step 219: continuation 0.8151, exact copy 0.2222 (20/90). Independence predicts 18.8/90.
Later checkpoint: continuation 0.8300, exact copy 0.2111 (19/90). Independence predicts 21.6/90.

The standard deviation of a 90-case exact-copy rate near 0.22 is about 3.9 cases, so both observations sit inside noise around their predictions, and the higher-continuation checkpoint is the better estimate of the underlying model.
findings.consequence: Leading the selection key with a 90-case count re-creates the v0.0.25 resolution problem one order of magnitude down. Selection needs a continuous statistic.

findings.claim: No higher-resolution discrete signal exists, because teacher-forced completion and greedy exact copy are the same event.
evidence: If the argmax is correct at every target position given the correct prefix, greedy decoding follows exactly that path and reproduces the string; the converse holds too.
Clean-stop is 1.0, so EOS handling does not separate the two.
findings.consequence: A lower-variance selector must be continuous: margins or sequence log-probabilities, not another pass/fail count.

findings.claim: The loss has never applied sequence-level pressure, which is the specific reason continuation gains do not convert into exact copies.
evidence: v0.0.20's margin term, carried into v0.0.26, averages the hinge over every copy token in the batch.
A sequence with one bad position and seven good ones therefore receives one eighth of the gradient pressure that its single failing position needs.
Under independence the marginal value of repairing each sequence's worst position is far higher than that of improving already-correct positions.
findings.consequence: A worst-position (min-margin) sequence term is the single best-aimed next change, and it is orthogonal to everything v0.0.26 changed.

recommended_next_phase.strategy: sequence-completion repair from the v0.0.26 best checkpoint
notes: Keep the v0.0.26 curriculum and the 1.2e-6 learning rate unchanged; change the objective only.
Add a worst-position hinge so each sequence's weakest copy token carries the gradient.
Reinstate hard mining, now scored by whole-sequence failure rather than mean token error; it was removed for v0.0.26 because it oversampled the wrong templates, which no longer applies.
Select checkpoints on a continuous sequence-margin statistic, with exact copy as a tiebreak, so a one-case fluctuation cannot pick the worse model.
Report exact copy bucketed by continuation length, so v0.0.28 knows whether the remaining failures are long sequences or specific kinds.
Separate promotion from progress in the report. v0.0.26 was a clear advance that reported only FAIL.
